xna-type.name: Cue
xna-type.summary: Defines methods for managing the playback of sounds.
xna-type.remarks: Cues are what programmers use to play sounds. Cues are typically played when certain game events occur, such as footsteps or gunshots. A cue is composed of one or more sounds, so when the cue is triggered, the set of associated sounds is heard. A sound specifies how one or more waves should be played. A sound also has specific properties such as volume and pitch. The sound designer can adjust these properties. The advantage to using the Audio API to reference cues rather than specific sounds is that an audio designer can reassign sounds to a cue in the sound bank without programmer intervention. For example, a sound designer can try various gunshot waves associated with a particular game event without requiring the programmer to change code or rename sounds. Cues and sounds are referenced through SoundBank objects. The waves that compose a sound are referenced through WaveBank objects.

property.name: IsCreated
property.summary: Returns whether the cue has been created.

property.name: IsDisposed
property.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the object has been disposed.

property.name: IsPaused
property.summary: Returns whether the cue is currently paused.
property.remarks: IsPlaying and IsPaused both return true if a cue is paused while playing.

property.name: IsPlaying
property.summary: Returns whether the cue is playing.
property.remarks: IsPlaying and IsPaused both return true if a cue is paused while playing.

property.name: IsPrepared
property.summary: Returns whether the cue is prepared to play.
property.remarks: This property returns true only if the cue is prepared but has not yet been played. Cues that are played return true for IsPlaying if they are currently playing or true for IsStopped if they are stopped.

property.name: IsPreparing
property.summary: Returns whether the cue is preparing to play.

property.name: IsStopped
property.summary: Returns whether the cue is currently stopped.

property.name: IsStopping
property.summary: Returns whether the cue is stopping playback.

property.name: Name
property.summary: Returns the friendly name of the cue.

method.name: Apply3D
method.summary: Calculates the 3D audio values between an AudioEmitter and an AudioListener object, and applies the resulting values to this Cue.

overload.summary: Calculates the 3D audio values between an AudioEmitter and an AudioListener object, and applies the resulting values to this Cue.
overload.remarks: If you want to apply 3D effects to a Cue , you must call this method before you call the Play method. Not doing so will throw an exception the next time Apply3D is called. Calling this method automatically sets the speaker mix for any sound played by this cue to a value calculated by the difference in Position values between listener and emitter . In preparation for the mix, the sound is converted to monoaural. Any stereo information in the sound is discarded. Calling this method sets the cue-instance variables Distance , DopplerPitchScalar , and OrientationAngle to the resulting values of the 3D calculation between listener and emitter . These values do not modify sound attenuation over distance, or pitch shifting via Doppler values, on their own. You must set up a Runtime Parameter Curve (RPC) that defines how to map the cue-instance variable values to pitch and volume shifts, and associate sounds to these curves in the Microsoft Cross-Platform Audio Creation Tool (XACT).

method.name: Dispose
method.summary: Immediately releases the unmanaged resources used by this object.

overload.summary: Immediately releases the unmanaged resources used by this object.

method.name: Equals
method.summary: Returns a value that indicates whether the current instance is equal to a specified object.

overload.summary: Returns a value that indicates whether the current instance is equal to a specified object.
overload.returns: true if the objects are the same; false otherwise.

method.name: GetHashCode
method.summary: Gets the hash code for this instance.

overload.summary: Gets the hash code for this instance.

method.name: GetVariable
method.summary: Gets a cue-instance variable value based on its friendly name.

overload.summary: Gets a cue-instance variable value based on its friendly name.
overload.remarks: Cue-instance variables are useful when multiple instantiations of a single cue (and its associated sounds) are required (for example, a "car" cue where there may be more than one car at any given time). While a global variable allows multiple audio elements to be controlled in unison, a cue instance variable grants discrete control of each instance of a cue, even for each copy of the same cue.

method.name: Play
method.summary: Requests playback of a prepared or preparing Cue.

overload.summary: Requests playback of a prepared or preparing Cue.

method.name: Resume
method.summary: Resumes playback of a paused Cue.

overload.summary: Resumes playback of a paused Cue.

method.name: SetVariable
method.summary: Sets the value of a cue-instance variable based on its friendly name.

overload.summary: Sets the value of a cue-instance variable based on its friendly name.

parameters.parameter: Friendly name of the variable to set.
Value to assign to the variable.

Enumerated value specifying how the sound should stop. If set to None , the sound will play any release phase or transition specified in the audio designer. If set to Immediate , the sound will stop immediately, ignoring any release phases or transitions.

event.summary: Occurs when Dispose is called or when this object is finalized and collected by the garbage collector of the Microsoft .NET common language runtime (CLR).
